The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000,00/- for the death of Suresh Kumar V.P. in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. That on 24.9.2023 at about 8.45 a.m. deceased Suresh Kumar V.P. was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-03-JZ-8148 on Vignan Nagar main road,
when he was extreme left side of the road, near Durgalakshmi Residency Apartment,
at that time, driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-03-MY-2948 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to which, Suresh Kumar sustained grievous injuries and died at Lakshmi Hospital.

Thereafter, post mortem was conducted at Sri. C.V.Raman Nagar Hospital,
Indiranagar, Bengaluru and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Subsequently, the petitioners have spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral, obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy,
aged about 46 years, working as a Bank Manager at HDFC Bank, Nrupathunga Road,
Bengaluru and earning Rs.1,50,000/- per month and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family. Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the Deepa P Nair vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130157981/
2 petitioners became dark, miserable and put to great financial hardship.
4.

sentences.text: It is contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-03-MY-2948.
In this regard, Jeevan Bhima Nagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said vehicle in Crime No.251/2023.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to the notice, respondents have appeared through their respective counsel and respondent No.1 has filed its written statement.
Inspite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.2 has not filed his written statement.
6. In the written statement, the respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing registration No.KA-03-MY-2948 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that, the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that, the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Further contended that 4th petitioner is not a dependent.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

7. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are legal heirs of deceased Suresh Kumar V.P. ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that Suresh Kumar V.P. sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent act of driver of car bearing No.KA-03-MY-2948 dated 24.9.2023 at about 8.45 a.m. and succumbed to injuries?

3) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, at what is the quantum from whom?
4) What order or award?
8.

Further examined Manager of the HDFC Bank Deepa P Nair vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130157981/

My findings to the above issues as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

 R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.2:-
12.
It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-03-MY- 2948, the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Suresh Kumar V.P. died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.
13. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

14. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
15. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Deepa P.Nair got examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon the police documents at Ex.
P1 to Ex
On going through the documents, Ex.P1- true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.251/2023 of Jeevan Bhima Nagar Traffic Police Station.

17. On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by Sanjeevkumar, the S.H.O. of Jeevan Bhima Nagar P.S. have registered the case Deepa P Nair vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130157981/

Upon investigation,
the I.O. has filed charge sheet against driver of the car alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
18.
On the other hand, though the respondent No.2 has taken contention that the accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the car.
In this regard he has examined driver of the offending vehicle as RW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
He has placed Aadhar card and D.L. at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
In the cross-examination he has admitted that his vehicle was damaged.
Though the driver of the offending vehicle examined but failed to establish his defence about the allegation made against him.

19. PW1 was subjected for cross-examination, but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
20. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-03-MY-2948 and in the said accident, Suresh Kumar V.P. succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.2 is in the Affirmative.
ISSUE No.1 & 3:
21.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P25 to Ex.P31 i.e., Aadhar card of deceased, PAN card of deceased and Aadhar cards of the petitioners have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.
22. At the time of arguments the counsel for the respondent No.1 has argued that the petitioner No.4 is the sister of the deceased and married, hence, she is not the dependent of the deceased.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW1, she has clearly stated that the petitioner No.4 is her sister-in-law and she is residing with her husband.
Hence, petitioner No.4 shall not be considered as dependent of the deceased.

23. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 being the wife has lost Deepa P Nair vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130157981/
5

sentences.text: her husband and the petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased have lost the love and affection of his father, petitioner No.3 is the father of deceased, who lost his son in his old age, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioner No.1 to 3 were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
24. The petitioners herein, have placed SSLC marks card, which is marked at Ex.P9 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 20.3.1977.
The accident occurred on 24.9.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 46 years.

For his age, multiplier '13' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma"
Case.
25.

In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as Bank Manager at HDFC,
Nrupathunga Road, Bengaluru and was earning Rs.1,50,000/- per month.

To prove the said aspect the petitioners have placed SSLC Marks card, Commerce certificate,
PUC Marks card, Degree marks card, M.Com., marks card, Computer certificate,
appointment letter, bonus document, appreciation letter, bonus statement, salary certificate, bank statement, form No.16 and I.D. card at Ex.P9 to Ex.P24.
26.
Further the petitioners have examined Bank Manager, HDFC Bank Ltd., as PW2.
He has deposed in his evidence that the deceased was permanent employee at their company and his employee code is S27590.
He was working as a Manager in their Organisation from February 2016 to till his death.
He was drawing salary of Rs.71,370/- per month.

If he would have been alive and continued his job he would have certainly got excellent appraisals and yearly increments of about 20%,
promotions and his gross salary would have been increased.
He has placed employment ID card and pay slip statement for the financial year from April 2023 to March 2024 at Ex.P32 & Ex.P33.
In the cross-examination he has admitted that he is in personal department.
In HDFC bank accounts department is there, but he is not working in the said department.

He had no information regarding Ex.P33.
27.

On perusal of Ex.P33, only basic pay and house rent allowance and medical allowance shall be considered, remaining allowances shall not considered as there is no details regarding the other income of the deceased.

Hence, by considering the August monthly basic pay of Rs.30,860/- + HRA of Rs.6,750/- + Medical allowance of Rs.1,250/- in toto it comes to Rs.38,860/- and after deducting professional tax of Rs.200/- and income tax at Rs.2,300/- it comes to Rs.36,360/- actual income of the deceased per month.

28. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, " It was observed that, "While determining the Deepa P Nair vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130157981/
6 income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

entities.text: 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Deepa P Nair vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

29. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
30.
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are three persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
31. In the present case, deceased was aged about 46 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "13" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Sarlaverma's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was come under the purview of below 40 years, 50% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.36,360/- per month, the annual income is of Rs.4,36,320/-.

Along with this, the future prospects of 50% is to be taken in to consideration,
then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.4,36,320+2,18,160) = Rs.6,54,480/-.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus,
net loss of income comes to Rs.4,36,320/- (Rs.6,54,480-Rs.2,18,160).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "13" which comes to Rs.56,72,160/-.
32.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others,

The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the Deepa P Nair vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130157981/
7 claimants for compensation.

entities.text: Deepa P Nair vs National Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

33. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 3 under the head loss of consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 34. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.

Compensation heads Compensation  Amount  Towards loss of Rs.56,72,160-00  dependency  Towards loss of Rs. 1,32,000-00  consortium  Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,500-00  Towards funeral & Rs. 16,500-00  obsequies ceremony  expenses  Total Rs.58,37,160-00 35.

Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.58,37,160/-
(Rupees fifty eight lakhs thirty seven thousand one hundred and sixty only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016, between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S.
Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

LIABILITY:
36.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-03-MY-2948,
alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent Deepa P Nair vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130157981/
8 No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

entities.text: Deepa P Nair vs National Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 37. As per records insurance policy was valid from 5.7.2023 to 4.7.2024.
The alleged accident had taken place on 24.9.2023.
As such, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.1 is in the Affirmative and the issue No.3 is Partly Affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
38.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.58,37,160/- (Rupees fifty eight lakhs thirty seven thousand one hundred and sixty only) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 60%, the petitioner No.2 is entitled the share of 35% and the petitioner No.3 is entitled the share of 5%.
The petitioner No.4 is not entitled for any compensation as she is not considered as dependent of the deceased.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1, 40% of her share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% of her share shall be released in favour of them through due process of law.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.2, being minor,
entire amount shall be deposited in any Nationalised/Scheduled bank till he attains age of majority.
After attaining the age of majority, entire amount shall be released to him through due process of law.
The guardian of the petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.3, by considering the age of the petitioner, entire amount shall be released to him through due process of law.
